syllabus.quote: Discuss write about issue(s) or topic(s) in depth in a structured way

one_line: Write full sentences in paragraphs that give at least two benefits and at least two drawbacks of the thing in the question, and expand every point with a 'because' or 'so'.

points.text: Marks go to points from a list. A point is often worth 1 mark, and a second mark comes when you expand it: the mark scheme shows the point as (1st) and the expansion as (1). A bare point with no expansion leaves marks behind.

cites.quote: Direct data source/direct data is reliable/trusted (1st) – because we collected it (1)
Orders are/can be processed straight away (1st) • so process of filling/completing orders can start sooner (than for batch processing) (1)
Must have expansions or comparisons to be a proper discussion

points.text: Each side has a ceiling. In the 2022-2025 mark schemes I checked (77 Discuss parts in cw_parts.json), 35 print a separate MAX for each side; for 8-mark questions it is usually MAX 6 (sometimes 5, once 7). So an answer with only benefits can never reach 8.

cites.quote: This method gathers direct data, which is more up to date (1) Benefits max 6:
Disadvantages MAX five from
Content areas could include: Max SIX from: Benefits: e.g.:

points.text: One-sided answers are capped. Many 2022-2023 mark schemes (20 of the 77 I checked) say you need at least two of each side (one of each on 4- and 6-mark questions) for full marks. The 2023 and 2025 examiner reports say the same: no full marks without both sides.

cites.quote: Must have at least two of each to gain full marks Must be a proper discussion to obtain full marks
Answers that do not provide both do not access the highest marks because a proper discussion should look at both sides of an issue.
Also, where both benefits and drawbacks are required by the question, answers that address only benefits or only drawbacks cannot achieve full marks.

points.text: Sometimes there is one mark for a short opening definition of the thing in the question. I found it in 18 of the 77 mark schemes, nearly always capped at one mark (two once). So one clear opening sentence can help, but a long introduction cannot earn more.

cites.quote: One mark from: • Definition of encryption (1) Max 6 from: Benefits:
Max one for: • Definition of computer simulation (1) Max six from: Benefits
Eight from: Simple statement of the difference between the two (1): e.g.

points.text: No 2022-2025 Discuss mark scheme I checked has a mark for a conclusion or your opinion. The current syllabus meaning of Discuss does not ask for one. Older reports (2019) used an older wording that said Discuss often needs a conclusion; that is no longer how it is defined. A one-line conclusion does no harm, but put your time into expanded points.

cites.quote: Discuss write about issue(s) or topic(s) in depth in a structured way
Discuss questions require candidates to give the important arguments for and against, and often require a conclusion.

points.text: Bullet points cost marks. Every 2022 and 2023 Discuss mark scheme (and some in 2024) caps a bulleted list: max 6 of 8, max 4 of 6, max 3 of 4. I counted 48 of the 77 mark schemes with this cap.

cites.quote: Max. six marks if bullets/list of points Must have expansions or comparisons to be a proper discussion
Must be at least one of each for full marks. Max 4 marks if bullets/list of points.
Must have at least one of each to gain full marks Max. three marks if bullets/list of points

points.text: The 2025 mark schemes no longer print the bullet cap, but the examiners still say lists and tables of statements cannot reach most of the marks. This includes two separate lists (benefits, then drawbacks) made of single words or very short sentences.

cites.quote: so learners who produced bulleted lists or tables of statements were unable to access most of the marks.

The command word ‘discuss’ requires candidates to provide a structured answer, so a bulleted list of brief statements is not properly answering the question and does not gain access to the full range of marks.
This comment also applies to answers that have separate lists of benefits and drawbacks, but the lists consist of single word or very brief sentences.

points.text: Write in full sentences and continuous prose. A good shape is one paragraph of benefits and one of drawbacks, with each point followed by its reason or effect in the same sentence.

cites.quote: Candidates should be encouraged to write answers in full sentences.
Questions that ask candidates to discuss the benefits and drawbacks of something require responses to give both sides of the argument and should be in continuous prose rather than bullet points.
The strongest answers were written in full prose style and included points which were expanded upon

points.text: Making a point and stopping. Examiners say most students give valid points but few expand them, and some mark schemes cap answers with no expansion at 6 of 8.

cites.quote: Most responses gained credit for making valid points, but few went on to discuss the points they made by expanding on them.
Max. six marks if bullets/list of points Max six marks if no attempt at expansion

points.text: Vague cost words. Writing that something is 'expensive' or 'costs more' was too vague. Say what the money is spent on (for example travel, printing questionnaires, cooling systems).

cites.quote: Where candidates stated that collecting direct data was expensive, this was considered too vague, but if candidates identified an area on which money would have to be spent, which would not otherwise be spent, this was awarded.
Many responses mentioned costs without going into sufficient detail to merit credit.

points.text: Writing the same point twice, once as a benefit and again reversed as a drawback. It earns only once and wastes time.

cites.quote: Some candidates effectively wrote what was good about direct data compared to indirect data and then repeated the list, but in reverse structure, so the positive aspects of one became the negative points of the other.
(Converse answer may also be given as an advantage – Award ONCE only)

points.text: Describing the topic instead of discussing it in the question's setting. Describing types of technology, or the stages of a process, or writing about the wrong context, gained little or nothing. Tie each benefit and drawback to the people or organisation named in the question.

cites.quote: Descriptions of different types of TEL, statements about benefits or drawbacks gained little or no credit without further comment on how these can affect the achievement of students.
there were many who made mistakes such as describing the stages of the data mining process or confusing data mining with another topic altogether
Answers should have focused on how banking organisations make use of data mining.

question.quote: Data can be collected by using a direct or an indirect data source. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using direct data compared to indirect data.

strong.sentence: Direct data is collected first-hand by the person who will use it (a primary source), while indirect data was collected by someone else for another purpose (a secondary source).

earns.quote: Simple statement of the difference between the two (1): e.g.

strong.sentence: One advantage of direct data is that it is more reliable and trusted, because we collected it ourselves and know exactly how it was gathered.

earns.quote: Direct data source/direct data is reliable/trusted (1st) – because we collected it (1)

strong.sentence: Also, only specific, relevant data is collected, so time is not wasted sorting through data we do not need.
Direct data is also more up to date than indirect data, which may have been collected years ago.

earns.quote: Direct data is (more) up-to-date (1) Disadvantages MAX SIX

strong.sentence: However, a disadvantage is that the sample size may be small, whereas indirect data sources tend to be much larger sets of data.

earns.quote: The sample size may be small (1st) – whereas indirect data sources tend to be larger sets of data (1)

strong.sentence: Collecting direct data also costs money that would not otherwise be spent, such as travelling to interview people and printing questionnaires.

earns.quote: Collecting direct data involves the expense of travelling/photocopying/printing questionnaires//any expense to do with a direct data method (1)

weak.answer: Advantages: direct data is cheaper, relevant, up to date. Disadvantages: indirect data is not relevant and old, direct data is expensive.
weak.why: It is a list, not a discussion. 'Expensive' does not say what the money is spent on. The disadvantages just repeat the advantages in reverse, so they earn nothing new.

basis.quote: Some candidates effectively wrote what was good about direct data compared to indirect data and then repeated the list, but in reverse structure, so the positive aspects of one became the negative points of the other.

examples.note: Six sentences earn eight marks because two of them carry a point plus its expansion. The examiner report says this question did not need both sides of the direct/indirect comparison, so do not write each point twice in reverse.

question.quote: Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of using data mining in businesses.

strong.sentence: Data mining is the use of software tools to analyse very large data sets.

earns.quote: data mining (is a set of techniques and tools) used to from work on / analyse large data sets

strong.sentence: Its aim is to discover trends, patterns and relationships in the data that people would not spot by hand.

earns.quote: to discover trends / patterns / to find relationships

strong.sentence: A business can use data mining to improve its sales and profits, because it can target its advertising at the customers or demographic groups most likely to buy.

earns.quote: used to improve sales / profits (1st) by targeting customers / demographics (1)

strong.sentence: The information it extracts also gives managers a sound basis for their decisions, rather than guesswork.

earns.quote: (usually) extracts reliable information • provides a sound basis for decision-making

strong.sentence: On the other hand, the extracted information may not be accurate, because it depends on how good the source data set is.

earns.quote: extracted information may not be accurate (1st) depends on source of data set (1)

strong.sentence: The business must also protect the privacy of the individuals in the data and follow data protection laws, which adds work and risk.

earns.quote: must ensure privacy of individuals / conform to data protection regulations

weak.answer: A two-column table: Benefits | Drawbacks; trends | expensive; profit | privacy; decisions | storage.
weak.why: Single words in a table make points but give no reasons or effects, so there is no discussion and no expansion marks.

basis.quote: Furthermore, if these answers are shown in a sketched table, they do not properly answer the question as there is no discussion.

examples.note: This 2025 mark scheme allowed up to two marks for saying what data mining is, then MAX SIX per side. Two expanded benefits and two drawbacks in sentences, plus a definition, reach eight.

thin_evidence: Not thin: Discuss appears in 80 question parts from 2022 onward (77 with mark schemes available). The counts above are my own regex counts over the mark-scheme text in cw_parts.json and could be off by one or two.
